title: [Model loader]: support multi-thread model weight loading (#23928)

image.wheel_note: first PyPI release after merge (2025-09-13 > 2025-09-09); picked by gen_tasks.py from PyPI upload dates.

workload.note: Weight-shard iteration over 8 synthetic 128 MB bf16 safetensors files (1 GB, written to a temp dir, page-cached): PR's solution = multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator (8 workers), baseline tree lacks it so the bench runs the single-thread safetensors_weights_iterator the loader uses there. Seconds per full pass, best of 3. Author: QwQ-32B 62 GB load 20 s -> 14 s (reported-only). Opt-in feature (enable_multithread_load).

policy.one_run_is: one `docker run` of the workload cmd per arm per repeat (same image, arm tree swapped in by the prelude)

contention_gate.rules: wait while another tenant uses the GPU (>5 % util or a foreign compute process >1 GiB) or the CPU (load1 > nproc/2)

policy.machine_snapshot: machine.py snapshot per workload run -> data/pr_<n>/work/machine_<arm>_<i>.json

arm_isolation.tree: wipe the wheel's vllm/*.py, copy the arm's vllm/ over site-packages (compiled .so stay)
arm_isolation.files: overlay ONLY task.json:source_files from the arm over the wheel's own tree
arm_isolation.tests_benchmarks: copied from the PR's merge tree to /t without a sibling vllm/ package

policy.noise_model: measure.py: paired log-speedup, MAD sigma, theta = clip(k*sigma, theta_min, theta_max) with k/theta from config.yaml:measure

metrics.name: model_load_time
metrics.parse: Load Time (not measured: QwQ-32B 62 GB, TP8, NVMe)

metrics.name: multi_thread_weight_loading

reported.scope: wall-clock weight Load Time for a 62 GB QwQ-32B model read from a single NVMe SSD with page cache dropped; the win is disk-bandwidth-bound (3.1 -> 4.42 GB/s) not compute
reported.scale_short: Author's 20->14s is for a 62 GB model streamed from a specific NVMe SSD with cold page cache; the gain depends entirely on the storage device's parallel-read bandwidth. TO MAKE 1:1: load a multi-shard safetensors model from the SAME class of NVMe with the page cache dropped, timing _get_weights_iterator with num_threads=1 vs 8; a tiny model or warm page cache collapses the gap (author saw only ~0.2s from cache).
reported.scale_note: This is CPU/IO-measurable later but NOT GPU-dependent. The speedup is purely from parallelizing shard reads to saturate NVMe bandwidth; the author confirmed in comments that with a warm page cache the improvement shrinks to ~0.2s, so magnitude is highly storage- and model-size-dependent. Direction is genuine for cold large-model loads from fast disks.

metrics.note: Diff adds multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator and multi_thread_pt_weights_iterator (concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor over shard files) in weight_utils.py, and DefaultModelLoader selects them when enable_multithread_load is set (num_threads default 8); also validates extra-config keys. Number source: PR body Test Result table - disable 20 s / 3.1 GB/s vs enable 14 s / 4.42 GB/s, 'Load Weight speed up 1.43x'.
